newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada agency says grounded WestJet for safety.
newsitem.headline: Canada agency says grounded WestJet for safety.

text.p: Transport Canada, the country's main transportation regulator, said on Tuesday it grounded no-frills carrier WestJet Airlines' four plane fleet for safety reasons.
"Safety is Transport Canada's first priority," Canadian Transport Minister David Anderson said in a statement. "We are acting today out of an abundance of caution."
Calgary-based WestJet announced Tuesday that all of its flights were grounded after a maintenance dispute with Transport Canada.

The company said it would retain legal counsel and immediately begin a lawsuit against the Canadian government over the conflict, which is expected to keep its fleet out of western Canadian skies until October 17.
Transport Canada said WestJet must appoint a qualified person to be responsible for aircraft maintenance and implement an agency-approved maintenance system within 15 days.
If the company does not comply, its operating certificate will be suspended, the agency said.
It said a scheduled audit, which is done six months following the startup of a new airline, was under way and WestJet was cooperating.
As a result of preliminary findings, the company voluntarily ceased flight operations, Transport Canada said.

WestJet said Tuesday that Transport Canada told the company on September 9 that its maintenance program did not meet terms in an "alternate maintenance document," which was different from a previously approved manual.
The company said it volunteered at the time to change its maintenance program to comply with the alternate document, but would take some time to make the transition.
No such time was granted, the company said. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
